extraction.body: Strategy’s enterprise mNAV fell below 1, putting its valuation under bitcoin reserves. The market is valuing Strategy below its bitcoin reserves: the company’s enterprise mNAV fell below 1, Reuters reported . In December 2025, the market had already valued the company’s market cap below the value of its BTC reserves, but that was based on basic mNAV. The metric compares a company’s market capitalization with the amount of digital assets on its balance sheet. Enterprise mNAV reflects the entire capital structure: common equity market cap, debt, perpetual preferreds, and the dollar reserve. As MSTR fell to around $82, the company’s value declined to $50.4 billion. With bitcoin near $60,000, Strategy’s bitcoin reserves were valued at roughly $51.1 billion. “At these levels, issuing new shares becomes dilutive, as the company would effectively be selling equity at a price below the value of its underlying assets,” CoinDesk noted. The premium to bitcoin reserves has been central to Strategy’s model. While the shares traded well above the value of BTC on the balance sheet, the company could issue new stock, buy the asset, and increase its per-share figure. When enterprise mNAV drops below 1, the firm still has access to other capital management tools, including debt, preferreds, refinancing, and cash flow from its core business. However, issuing common stock at such levels can increase pressure on shareholders due to dilution. Reuters cited a December statement by Strategy CEO Fong Le. He said the company may consider selling bitcoin if mNAV falls below 1 and other sources of capital are exhausted. Le described this as a last resort rather than a change in policy. Between May 26 and May 31, Strategy sold 32 BTC for roughly $2.5 million at an average price of $77,135 per coin. According to the official purchases table , as of June 22 Strategy held 847,363 BTC. The aggregate acquisition cost was $64.1 billion, with an average purchase price of $75,651 per coin. The latest disclosed purchase was during June 15–21: the company acquired 520 BTC for about $35 million at an average price of $67,068. Before that, Strategy bought 1,587 BTC during June 8–14 and 1,550 BTC during June 1–7. With bitcoin below $60,000, the company’s position is under its average purchase price. Reuters valued Strategy’s reserve at roughly $50.4 billion based on Sunday’s bitcoin close at $59,577.82. The issue is not limited to common shares. In 2026, Strategy actively used perpetual preferred securities, including STRC, to finance bitcoin purchases. Against this backdrop, STRC also came under pressure. On Friday the securities fell to a new low around $71.40, then recovered to $74.72. That is about 26% below the $100 par value. With STRC around $73, the securities’ effective yield approached 15%, increasing expectations of a dividend rate hike, The Block wrote. On June 23, Strategy filed with the SEC to move STRC to semi-monthly distributions. On June 29, Saylor presented a capital framework for digital credit instruments. It is aimed at supporting liquidity, preserving long-term bitcoin exposure, and managing obligations to holders of such securities. As part of the new policy, Strategy increased its dollar reserve to $2.55 billion. According to the company, this covers 17.4 months of expected preferred dividend payments and interest expense. The minimum reserve level is set at 12 months of such obligations. The company also raised the annual dividend rate on STRC by 50 basis points to 12%. The change takes effect in July 2026. Strategy will evaluate the rate monthly, considering the price of STRC, market yields, credit spreads, bitcoin’s price and volatility, dollar-reserve coverage, and the overall capital structure. Separately, Strategy’s board authorized a bitcoin monetization program. It allows the company to sell bitcoin to top up the dollar reserve by up to $1.25 billion, pay dividends and interest, and repurchase credit instruments and MSTR shares. Strategy also approved buyback programs of up to $1 billion each: for credit instruments including STRC, STRF, STRD and STRK, and for Class A common shares. The company emphasized that such repurchases will not be funded from the dollar reserve. As The Block noted, other companies using the bitcoin-treasury model are also under pressure. Japanese Metaplanet’s enterprise mNAV was about 0.9, and Nakamoto, backed by David Bailey, about 0.92. Strive is an exception. According to BitcoinTreasuries , its enterprise mNAV was around 1.24. Coin Bureau founder Nik Pakrin told Reuters the development is “bad news for overall investor sentiment toward cryptocurrencies and bitcoin.” “MSTR was that one digital treasury company investors continued to believe in, but that belief is now eroding. We are already seeing it in the price of bitcoin,” he said. In June, Strategy founder Michael Saylor presented the “digital asset stack” concept. In his view, bitcoin will evolve from a simple asset into the foundation of global financial architecture. At the end of the month, CEO Ripple Brad Garlinghouse called the model harmful for the market ; it finances cryptocurrency purchases by issuing preferred stock. coreStoryFacts.text: Nov 20 (Reuters) - Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency, fell below the $60,000 level on Friday for the first time since July, as lofty valuation concerns weighed on the AI trade and other risk assets.
Ether, the second-largest cryptocurrency, was down 5.23% at $1,648.91.
Strategy’s enterprise mNAV fell below 1, putting its valuation under bitcoin reserves.
As MSTR fell to around $82, the company’s value declined to $50.4 billion.
While the shares traded well above the value of BTC on the balance sheet, the company could issue new stock, buy the asset, and increase its per-share figure.
Separately, Strategy’s board authorized a bitcoin monetization program.
It allows the company to sell bitcoin to top up the dollar reserve by up to $1.25 billion, pay dividends and interest, and repurchase credit instruments and MSTR shares.
He said the company may consider selling bitcoin if mNAV falls below 1 and other sources of capital are exhausted.
The company also raised the annual dividend rate on STRC by 50 basis points to 12%.
Strategy will evaluate the rate monthly, considering the price of STRC, market yields, credit spreads, bitcoin’s price and volatility, dollar-reserve coverage, and the overall capital structure.
As part of the new policy, Strategy increased its dollar reserve to $2.55 billion.
The minimum reserve level is set at 12 months of such obligations.
In 2026, Strategy actively used perpetual preferred securities, including STRC, to finance bitcoin purchases.
On June 23, Strategy filed with the SEC to move STRC to semi-monthly distributions.
On June 29, Saylor presented a capital framework for digital credit instruments.
It is aimed at supporting liquidity, preserving long-term bitcoin exposure, and managing obligations to holders of such securities.
Analysts Support Strategy’s Shift from Pure Bitcoin Reserves
Between May 26 and May 31, Strategy sold 32 BTC for roughly $2.5 million at an average price of $77,135 per coin.
According to the official purchases table , as of June 22 Strategy held 847,363 BTC.
Before that, Strategy bought 1,587 BTC during June 8–14 and 1,550 BTC during June 1–7.
In June, Strategy founder Michael Saylor presented the “digital asset stack” concept.
In his view, bitcoin will evolve from a simple asset into the foundation of global financial architecture.
Michael Saylor Asserts Strategy Will Withstand Bitcoin’s Fall to $8000
Investors accuse JPMorgan of targeting Michael Saylor’s Strategy

story.title: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 level - Reuters

facts.text: Nov 20 (Reuters) - Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency, fell below the $60,000 level on Friday for the first time since July, as lofty valuation concerns weighed on the AI trade and other risk assets.
Ether, the second-largest cryptocurrency, was down 5.23% at $1,648.91.
Strategy’s enterprise mNAV fell below 1, putting its valuation under bitcoin reserves.
As MSTR fell to around $82, the company’s value declined to $50.4 billion.
While the shares traded well above the value of BTC on the balance sheet, the company could issue new stock, buy the asset, and increase its per-share figure.
Separately, Strategy’s board authorized a bitcoin monetization program.
It allows the company to sell bitcoin to top up the dollar reserve by up to $1.25 billion, pay dividends and interest, and repurchase credit instruments and MSTR shares.
He said the company may consider selling bitcoin if mNAV falls below 1 and other sources of capital are exhausted.
The company also raised the annual dividend rate on STRC by 50 basis points to 12%.
Strategy will evaluate the rate monthly, considering the price of STRC, market yields, credit spreads, bitcoin’s price and volatility, dollar-reserve coverage, and the overall capital structure.
As part of the new policy, Strategy increased its dollar reserve to $2.55 billion.
The minimum reserve level is set at 12 months of such obligations.
In 2026, Strategy actively used perpetual preferred securities, including STRC, to finance bitcoin purchases.
On June 23, Strategy filed with the SEC to move STRC to semi-monthly distributions.
On June 29, Saylor presented a capital framework for digital credit instruments.
It is aimed at supporting liquidity, preserving long-term bitcoin exposure, and managing obligations to holders of such securities.

Between May 26 and May 31, Strategy sold 32 BTC for roughly $2.5 million at an average price of $77,135 per coin.
According to the official purchases table , as of June 22 Strategy held 847,363 BTC.
Before that, Strategy bought 1,587 BTC during June 8–14 and 1,550 BTC during June 1–7.
In June, Strategy founder Michael Saylor presented the “digital asset stack” concept.
In his view, bitcoin will evolve from a simple asset into the foundation of global financial architecture.

The market is valuing Strategy below its bitcoin reserves: the company’s enterprise mNAV fell below 1, Reuters reported . In December 2025, the market had already valued the company’s market cap below the value of its BTC reserves, but that was based on basic mNAV. The metric compares a company’s market capitalization with the amount of digital assets on its balance sheet. Enterprise mNAV reflects the entire capital structure: common equity market cap, debt, perpetual preferreds, and the dollar reserve. As MSTR fell to around $82, the company’s value declined to $50.4 billion. With bitcoin near $60,000, Strategy’s bitcoin reserves were valued at roughly $51.1 billion. “At these levels, issuing new shares becomes dilutive, as the company would effectively be selling equity at a price below the value of its underlying assets,” CoinDesk noted. The premium to bitcoin reserves has been central to Strategy’s model. While the shares traded well above the value of BTC on the balance sheet, the company could issue new stock, buy the asset, and increase its per-share figure. When enterprise mNAV drops below 1, the firm still has access to other capital management tools, including debt, preferreds, refinancing, and cash flow from its core business. However, issuing common stock at such levels can increase pressure on shareholders due to dilution. Reuters cited a December statement by Strategy CEO Fong Le. He said the company may consider selling bitcoin if mNAV falls below 1 and other sources of capital are exhausted. Le described this as a last resort rather than a change in policy. Between May 26 and May 31, Strategy sold 32 BTC for roughly $2.5 million at an average price of $77,135 per coin. According to the official purchases table , as of June 22 Strategy held 847,363 BTC. The aggregate acquisition cost was $64.1 billion, with an average purchase price of $75,651 per coin. The latest disclosed purchase was during June 15–21: the company acquired 520 BTC for about $35 million at an average price of $67,068. Before that, Strategy bought 1,587 BTC during June 8–14 and 1,550 BTC during June 1–7. With bitcoin below $60,000, the company’s position is under its average purchase price. Reuters valued Strategy’s reserve at roughly $50.4 billion based on Sunday’s bitcoin close at $59,577.82. The issue is not limited to common shares. In 2026, Strategy actively used perpetual preferred securities, including STRC, to finance bitcoin purchases. Against this backdrop, STRC also came under pressure. On Friday the securities fell to a new low around $71.40, then recovered to $74.72. That is about 26% below the $100 par value. With STRC around $73, the securities’ effective yield approached 15%, increasing expectations of a dividend rate hike, The Block wrote. On June 23, Strategy filed with the SEC to move STRC to semi-monthly distributions. On June 29, Saylor presented a capital framework for digital credit instruments. It is aimed at supporting liquidity, preserving long-term bitcoin exposure, and managing obligations to holders of such securities. As part of the new policy, Strategy increased its dollar reserve to $2.55 billion. According to the company, this covers 17.4 months of expected preferred dividend payments and interest expense. The minimum reserve level is set at 12 months of such obligations. The company also raised the annual dividend rate on STRC by 50 basis points to 12%. The change takes effect in July 2026. Strategy will evaluate the rate monthly, considering the price of STRC, market yields, credit spreads, bitcoin’s price and volatility, dollar-reserve coverage, and the overall capital structure. Separately, Strategy’s board authorized a bitcoin monetization program. It allows the company to sell bitcoin to top up the dollar reserve by up to $1.25 billion, pay dividends and interest, and repurchase credit instruments and MSTR shares. Strategy also approved buyback programs of up to $1 billion each: for credit instruments including STRC, STRF, STRD and STRK, and for Class A common shares. The company emphasized that such repurchases will not be funded from the dollar reserve. As The Block noted, other companies using the bitcoin-treasury model are also under pressure. Japanese Metaplanet’s enterprise mNAV was about 0.9, and Nakamoto, backed by David Bailey, about 0.92. Strive is an exception. According to BitcoinTreasuries , its enterprise mNAV was around 1.24. Coin Bureau founder Nik Pakrin told Reuters the development is “bad news for overall investor sentiment toward cryptocurrencies and bitcoin.” “MSTR was that one digital treasury company investors continued to believe in, but that belief is now eroding. We are already seeing it in the price of bitcoin,” he said. In June, Strategy founder Michael Saylor presented the “digital asset stack” concept. In his view, bitcoin will evolve from a simple asset into the foundation of global financial architecture. At the end of the month, CEO Ripple Brad Garlinghouse called the model harmful for the market ; it finances cryptocurrency purchases by issuing preferred stock. Ether, the second-largest cryptocurrency, was down 5.23% at $1,648.91.
Strategy’s enterprise mNAV fell below 1, putting its valuation under bitcoin reserves.
As MSTR fell to around $82, the company’s value declined to $50.4 billion.
While the shares traded well above the value of BTC on the balance sheet, the company could issue new stock, buy the asset, and increase its per-share figure.
Separately, Strategy’s board authorized a bitcoin monetization program.
It allows the company to sell bitcoin to top up the dollar reserve by up to $1.25 billion, pay dividends and interest, and repurchase credit instruments and MSTR shares.
He said the company may consider selling bitcoin if mNAV falls below 1 and other sources of capital are exhausted.
The company also raised the annual dividend rate on STRC by 50 basis points to 12%.
Strategy will evaluate the rate monthly, considering the price of STRC, market yields, credit spreads, bitcoin’s price and volatility, dollar-reserve coverage, and the overall capital structure.
As part of the new policy, Strategy increased its dollar reserve to $2.55 billion.
The minimum reserve level is set at 12 months of such obligations.
In 2026, Strategy actively used perpetual preferred securities, including STRC, to finance bitcoin purchases.
On June 23, Strategy filed with the SEC to move STRC to semi-monthly distributions.

The first flaw, CVE-2026-23871, affects WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before version 2.26.17.4. It involves incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs. An attacker could send media from an attacker-controlled URL in a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message. When WhatsApp displayed that message in a thread, the attacker could learn the target's IP address. WhatsApp said someone may have used the flaw with specific spam messages. The company's security team discovered and reported the issue. A WhatsApp spokesperson said the team found the flaw while disrupting a scam campaign and believes a scammer used it to make scam messages seem more credible. WhatsApp did not disclose the scale of the activity or whether those efforts succeeded. The second flaw, CVE-2026-102769, is an SQL injection vulnerability in WhatsApp for Android before version 2.26.35.74. It occurs when a recipient taps a crafted "order details" message sent from an unofficial client. The tap can delete files stored on the device. An attacker could learn one bit about the user's chat database through an induced-crash delivery receipt timing side channel if the user is online when the malicious message arrives. WhatsApp said it found no evidence that anyone exploited the flaw in the wild. The third flaw, CVE-2026-44908, is a trust-validation vulnerability in WhatsApp's certificate verification mechanism for Meta AI's confidential computing infrastructure. It affects WhatsApp for iOS before version 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp Business for iOS and WhatsApp for Mac Desktop before version 2.26.23.72, WhatsApp for Android before version 2.26.23.74, and WhatsApp Business for Android before version 2.26.23.70. An actor positioned inside Meta infrastructure could bypass the hardware root of trust with a Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificate not signed by the hardware manufacturer's key. Someone would first need to publish that certificate to the third-party binary transparency ledger that WhatsApp Private Processing uses. WhatsApp said the ledger shows every published VCEK certificate chains to the hardware root of trust, which confirms no exploitation. WhatsApp advises users to keep apps and devices updated. The company said it keeps strengthening its systems and acknowledged the bug bounty community's contributions to platform security. extraction.body: Meta-owned messaging platform WhatsApp has patched three security vulnerabilities affecting its Android, iOS and desktop applications, including a flaw suspected of being misused in connection with fraudulent messages. The vulnerabilities could potentially expose users’ IP information, delete locally stored files and weaken certificate verification protections associated with Meta AI infrastructure. One of the vulnerabilities, identified as CVE-2026-23871, was discovered by WhatsApp’s internal security team while investigating a scam campaign. The company suspects that the flaw was being used to make fraudulent messages appear more credible. WhatsApp has not disclosed the scale of the suspected activity or confirmed whether the exploitation attempts were successful. The company has advised users to keep their applications and devices updated to protect against the vulnerabilities. FCRF Launches Certified Chief Risk Officer (CRO) Program for India’s Risk Leaders The first vulnerability, CVE-2026-23871, affects WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android versions earlier than 2.26.17.4. The flaw, assigned a Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) severity score of 3.5, resulted from incomplete validation of external URLs associated with advertisements that allow users to initiate WhatsApp conversations. According to WhatsApp, an attacker could potentially cause a targeted device to disclose its IP information by sending media from an attacker-controlled URL through a specially crafted Click to WhatsApp advertisement reply message. The exposure could occur when the manipulated message was rendered and displayed in a conversation thread. WhatsApp said the vulnerability may have been abused alongside specific spam messages. The company confirmed that its security researchers identified the issue while disrupting a scam campaign. A spokesperson indicated that the suspected attacker may have used the vulnerability to make scam messages appear more trustworthy to recipients. However, WhatsApp did not provide details about the number of users potentially affected or whether the suspected exploitation resulted in successful fraud. The second vulnerability, CVE-2026-102769, is an SQL injection flaw affecting WhatsApp for Android versions earlier than 2.26.35.74. With a CVSS score of 6.8, the vulnerability could allow a specially crafted order details message sent through an unofficial WhatsApp client to trigger the deletion of locally stored WhatsApp files when the recipient tapped on the message. Researchers also found that the vulnerability could expose a limited amount of information through a timing-based side channel. According to WhatsApp, an attacker could potentially obtain one bit of information relating to a user’s chat database by analysing the timing of delivery receipts associated with an induced application crash. The company stated that there was no evidence of this vulnerability being exploited in real-world attacks. The third flaw, CVE-2026-44908, concerns improper trust validation within the certificate verification mechanism used by Meta AI’s confidential computing infrastructure. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 4.8 and affects certain older versions of WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android and iOS, as well as WhatsApp for Mac. Successful exploitation could theoretically have allowed an attacker positioned within Meta’s infrastructure to bypass hardware-based trust verification by using a Versioned Chip Endorsement Key certificate that was not signed by the hardware manufacturer’s key. However, WhatsApp stated that such certificates would first need to appear in a third-party binary transparency ledger used by its Private Processing infrastructure. The company said the ledger showed that all published certificates were properly linked to the hardware root of trust, indicating that the vulnerability had not been exploited. WhatsApp has addressed the vulnerabilities through software updates and advised users to install the latest available versions of its applications. The Android vulnerability associated with scam messages affects versions earlier than 2.26.17.4, while the SQL injection flaw affects versions earlier than 2.26.35.74. The certificate validation issue affects WhatsApp for iOS versions earlier than 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Mac versions earlier than 2.26.23.72, WhatsApp for Android versions earlier than 2.26.23.74, and WhatsApp Business for Android versions earlier than 2.26.23.70. The reported weaknesses highlight different areas of application security, ranging from the handling of external web addresses and specially crafted messages to the validation of certificates used in confidential computing environments. Although WhatsApp suspects that one vulnerability was associated with scam-related activity, the company has not confirmed successful exploitation. It has also reported no evidence of real-world exploitation involving the other two flaws. Users are advised to update WhatsApp through official application stores, avoid interacting with suspicious messages and exercise caution when receiving unexpected payment requests or messages containing unfamiliar links. WhatsApp said it continues to strengthen its security systems and acknowledged the contributions of its internal security researchers and the wider bug bounty community in identifying vulnerabilities. extraction.body: Meta-owned messaging platform WhatsApp has patched three security vulnerabilities affecting its Android, iOS and desktop applications, including a flaw suspected of being misused in connection with fraudulent messages. The vulnerabilities could potentially expose users’ IP information, delete locally stored files and weaken certificate verification protections associated with Meta AI infrastructure. One of the vulnerabilities, identified as CVE-2026-23871, was discovered by WhatsApp’s internal security team while investigating a scam campaign. The company suspects that the flaw was being used to make fraudulent messages appear more credible. WhatsApp has not disclosed the scale of the suspected activity or confirmed whether the exploitation attempts were successful. The company has advised users to keep their applications and devices updated to protect against the vulnerabilities. FCRF Launches Certified Chief Risk Officer (CRO) Program for India’s Risk Leaders The first vulnerability, CVE-2026-23871, affects WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android versions earlier than 2.26.17.4. The flaw, assigned a Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) severity score of 3.5, resulted from incomplete validation of external URLs associated with advertisements that allow users to initiate WhatsApp conversations. According to WhatsApp, an attacker could potentially cause a targeted device to disclose its IP information by sending media from an attacker-controlled URL through a specially crafted Click to WhatsApp advertisement reply message. The exposure could occur when the manipulated message was rendered and displayed in a conversation thread. WhatsApp said the vulnerability may have been abused alongside specific spam messages. The company confirmed that its security researchers identified the issue while disrupting a scam campaign. A spokesperson indicated that the suspected attacker may have used the vulnerability to make scam messages appear more trustworthy to recipients. However, WhatsApp did not provide details about the number of users potentially affected or whether the suspected exploitation resulted in successful fraud. The second vulnerability, CVE-2026-102769, is an SQL injection flaw affecting WhatsApp for Android versions earlier than 2.26.35.74. With a CVSS score of 6.8, the vulnerability could allow a specially crafted order details message sent through an unofficial WhatsApp client to trigger the deletion of locally stored WhatsApp files when the recipient tapped on the message. Researchers also found that the vulnerability could expose a limited amount of information through a timing-based side channel. According to WhatsApp, an attacker could potentially obtain one bit of information relating to a user’s chat database by analysing the timing of delivery receipts associated with an induced application crash. The company stated that there was no evidence of this vulnerability being exploited in real-world attacks. The third flaw, CVE-2026-44908, concerns improper trust validation within the certificate verification mechanism used by Meta AI’s confidential computing infrastructure. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 4.8 and affects certain older versions of WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android and iOS, as well as WhatsApp for Mac. Successful exploitation could theoretically have allowed an attacker positioned within Meta’s infrastructure to bypass hardware-based trust verification by using a Versioned Chip Endorsement Key certificate that was not signed by the hardware manufacturer’s key. However, WhatsApp stated that such certificates would first need to appear in a third-party binary transparency ledger used by its Private Processing infrastructure. The company said the ledger showed that all published certificates were properly linked to the hardware root of trust, indicating that the vulnerability had not been exploited. WhatsApp has addressed the vulnerabilities through software updates and advised users to install the latest available versions of its applications. The Android vulnerability associated with scam messages affects versions earlier than 2.26.17.4, while the SQL injection flaw affects versions earlier than 2.26.35.74. The certificate validation issue affects WhatsApp for iOS versions earlier than 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Mac versions earlier than 2.26.23.72, WhatsApp for Android versions earlier than 2.26.23.74, and WhatsApp Business for Android versions earlier than 2.26.23.70. The reported weaknesses highlight different areas of application security, ranging from the handling of external web addresses and specially crafted messages to the validation of certificates used in confidential computing environments. Although WhatsApp suspects that one vulnerability was associated with scam-related activity, the company has not confirmed successful exploitation. It has also reported no evidence of real-world exploitation involving the other two flaws. Users are advised to update WhatsApp through official application stores, avoid interacting with suspicious messages and exercise caution when receiving unexpected payment requests or messages containing unfamiliar links. WhatsApp said it continues to strengthen its security systems and acknowledged the contributions of its internal security researchers and the wider bug bounty community in identifying vulnerabilities. extraction.body: Bitcoin 's latest sell-off is reviving doubts that it can behave as the "digital gold" market hedge that crypto backers have long envisioned. Coming into 2026, experts said that showing bitcoin could serve as a market hedge rather than a risk-on asset that moves up and down with growth stocks was an important test for the cryptocurrency. Bitcoin was trading under $62,000 on Friday morning, down from an all-time high of more than $126,000 in early October last year. Its downward spiral in recent months and weeks has been precipitated by a confluence of factors. The heavy midterm elections losses for the Republicans, the Binance hack, and a world on edge about the security of all things technology — FAA ground stop, the outage of the National Security Agency's highly classified internal communications system, several online banking outages — have not helped the mood when it comes to putting trust in the digital world. But the market itself may be the biggest factor. Investors are currently in sell everything mode, including tech stocks and gold — the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 tumbled into correction territory on Friday, according to CNBC data. Bitcoin's recent price action has also tracked the move in the biggest tech IPOs , SpaceX and Anthropic. Taken together, the cryptocurrency is failing the test again when it comes to showing its worth as a market hedge during times of investor anxiety. In the past month alone, bitcoin had dropped roughly $20,000, as of Friday morning, according to CNBC data. Investors and financial management firms aren't viewing it as safe an investment as in the past, said Ryan Kirkley, co-founder and chief executive of Global Settlement Network, a Miami-based fintech that provides infrastructure for currency settlement, including crypto. "There's a bit more caution than there was a year ago." What is behind bitcoin's fall, and what is in store for its future? Here is what experts say. There have been many theories about how bitcoin would react based on different market and economic conditions. But historically, bitcoin has done best in low-rate environments and when lending opportunities are plentiful, said Juan Xavier Sanchez, head of wealth strategy at Activest Wealth Management in Aventura, Florida. When rates are down and treasuries aren't paying good yields, people tend to be more risk-seeking for higher returns. "Bitcoin for many investors is in that bucket," Sanchez said. Experts have noted that gold, which is now down over 35% from its early 2026 peak, is less attractive when cash accounts are paying 5%. Investments like gold and bitcoin offer no yield. Bitcoin's rising correlation with the Nasdaq-100 since late September suggests the two are increasingly moving in tandem, according to data from Fairlead Strategies, a technical research firm. That's consistent with an environment of higher volatility in which correlations across risk assets tend to increase. However, the correlation remains below its early-2026 highs, the data show. Bitcoin has certain characteristics of digital gold, in that it has a limited supply, no single owner and no CEO or board that can decide to issue more, said Anthony Georgiades, founder and general partner at Innovating Capital in New York, which invests in early-stage crypto, blockchain, digital infrastructure and deep tech companies. But it's also been caught up in monetary policy since its inception. The last decade or so of monetary policy has been extremely rewarding to speculative risk-on assets, Georgiades said. However, in periods of volatility, those types of assets have experienced the most significant drawdowns and have been the most heavily punished, Georgiades said. That means that a shock on one side of the board that might be completely independent of bitcoin could trigger a large volatility event "given how intertwined digital assets have become in the overall financial system," he said. Notably, bitcoin hasn't acted much like digital gold in more recent years, said Abe Sheikh, chief investment officer of Cordoba Advisory Partners in New York. In fact, it has fallen substantially during periods when the stock market has been falling. For example, from October 6 through November 18, the S&P 500 fell about 6.3%, and bitcoin fell around 27%. From January 21, 2025 through April 8, 2025, the S&P dropped around 17.4%, while bitcoin slid 27.8%, he said. Democrats gaining control over both houses is viewed as a negative for crypto from a market perspective. The crypto industry spent more than $200 million to support crypto-friendly candidates, but its role had less of an impact on overall results than in the last election cycle. However, bitcoin's downward trend was already in the works, said Cyrus Amini, chief investment officer at Hyphen Wealth Management in Lafayette, California. In September, the Clarity Act failed in the U.S. Senate, and while its outlook is now dim , according to many political and market experts, some form of crypto legislation is still considered a priority for many Democrats and Republicans, while the Trump-appointed heads of the Commodity Future Trading Commission and Securities and Exchange Commission continue to favor crypto in rulemaking. This fall, investors also started to question the security of encryption technology, leading to more concerns over the security of their bitcoin holdings, said Kirkley of Global Settlement Network. The Binance hack in October muddied the waters further. And the recent stock market jitters and economic concerns piled on doubts, Kirkley said. The last few weeks have been especially rough with data security concerns from multiple fronts, he added. Wall Street's embrace of bitcoin has been a big positive for the cryptocurrency. Kirkley noted that 20% of bitcoin's market price is coming from institutional investors, and that's a conservative estimate. In addition, new research from digital assets company Galaxy shows that a record 40.5% of all 13F-reported spot bitcoin exchange-traded product holdings, and 11.2% of all the bitcoin in the funds, came from advisory and wealth planning firms, such as RIAs and brokerage platforms, as of the third quarter 13F filings with the SEC, which are required of firms with over $100 million in assets to report their holdings. Much of this investment is through bitcoin spot ETFs like the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) that track its price. These ETFs, first approved by the SEC in January 2024, were supposed to provide a reliable new source of institutional demand. But ETF ownership also makes bitcoin especially easy to sell. Outflows from several of these funds have been substantial in recent months. IBIT, the largest of its peers, had six-month net outflows of $1.65 billion through Nov. 18 and one-month outflows of $1.37 billion, according to ETF Database. The second biggest, Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund ( FBTC ) had one-month net outflows of $322.65 million and six-month net outflows of $771.86 million, according to ETF Database. Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ETF ( BTC ) had one-month net outflows of $66.35 million, though it had inflows of $590.04 million over six months. As of September 2026, public companies collectively hold close to 1.29 million bitcoins, which is more than 6% of the 21 million coins in existence, according to bitcoin.com . Most public companies invest their corporate treasury portfolios in low-risk, highly liquid instruments such as money market funds, Treasury bonds and Treasury bills. That said, there are some well-known companies that have invested in bitcoin. SpaceX, for example, purchased 18,712 bitcoins for a total cost of $661 million, at an average price of $35,324 per coin. The company began accumulating bitcoin in early 2021 and held its position unchanged from mid-2024 until its IPO filing . Digital Asset Treasury companies, known as DATs or DATCOs, have also played a role in bitcoin's volatility . DATs are publicly listed firms whose primary business strategy involves holding significant quantities of digital assets, such as bitcoin or ethereum , on their corporate balance sheets to drive shareholder value. Companies in this space include Strategy , Strive, and Twenty One Capital. "DATs have exacerbated the problem," said Sheikh of Cordoba Advisory Partners. When bitcoin is rising, these companies borrow money in the debt market or raise capital to buy more bitcoin, which magnifies the upswings. They have also sold bitcoin to make their bond coupon payments. "It leads to enormous volatility on the upside and downside," Sheikh said. As of mid-November, Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, holds 850,849 BTC, according to a regulatory filing . That represents roughly 4% of bitcoin's total supply. The company acquired these holdings at a total cost of approximately $64.2 billion, with an average purchase price of roughly $75,452 per coin, according to the filing. Bitcoin has been trending lower since the peak in October 2025. A trading range has taken hold and the bottom of the range is just below 60,000, said Katie Stockton, founder and managing partner of Fairlead Strategies. "It appears to be trying to find a footing," she said. Oversold conditions on the heels of recent lows in June and July, in addition to long-term momentum, suggest bitcoin can support an upturn, she said. But that depends on whether the crypto can hold at a current range around $60,000, she said. "At the end of the day, bitcoin is exceptionally volatile. It's still an area that people might go to sell when they think that risk is higher in other areas." By mid-morning Friday, the price of bitcoin had slipped below $60,000, its lowest mark since July. It was on pace for its seventh-straight weekly loss for the first time since May 2022, according to CNBC data.

Sunday Guardian Live By: Zaini Majeed Last Updated: November 21, 2026 00:24:26 IST Bitcoin has plunged below the psychologically critical $60, 000 threshold to hit its weakest level since July, undermining long-standing claims that the world’s largest cryptocurrency functions as “digital gold” during periods of financial turbulence. Trading around $59, 170 on Friday, Bitcoin has shed roughly $20, 000 over the past month alone and now sits approximately 53 per cent below its October 2025 record high near $126, 000. Far from shielding investor portfolios from equity volatility, the digital asset broke lower shortly after the US market open alongside sharp losses in technology shares, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 2. 4 per cent and chipmaker Nvidia dropping 6 per cent. “The market appears to be trying to find a footing, ” Fairlead Strategies founder Katie Stockton said in a market note cited by financial outlets, pointing out that Bitcoin’s trading range has compressed to a floor just below $60, 000 as its correlation with the Nasdaq-100 climbed steadily since late September. Proponents of cryptocurrency have argued for years that Bitcoin’s capped supply of 21 million coins makes it an uncorrelated store of value capable of insulating investors from inflation and stock market drawdowns. Recent cross-asset trading, however, indicates that institutional desks continue to treat Bitcoin as a high-beta risk asset rather than a defensive refuge. Market data from Fairlead Strategies underscores that Bitcoin has moved largely in tandem with high-growth technology stocks throughout the autumn downturn. Even physical bullion faced acute liquidity pressure this week, with spot gold sliding more than 3 per cent to drop below $3, 700 per ounce as investors raised cash across asset classes to cover losses and margin requirements. Corporate treasury buyers that fuelled earlier rallies are also magnifying the downward volatility. Cordoba Advisory Partners chief investment officer Abe Sheikh told market analysts that companies such as Strategy, which holds 850, 849 BTC, roughly 4 per cent of total supply, borrow capital to accumulate Bitcoin during upswings and face pressure to offload holdings to service debt obligations when prices retreat. Institutional retreat from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds has removed a vital pillar of market support. According to figures compiled by Farside Investors, investors withdrew $582. 3 million from US spot Bitcoin funds on Thursday alone—including $541. 1 million from BlackRock’s flagship iShares fund—marking a third consecutive day of redemptions and pushing total November outflows to $3. 47 billion. Broader macroeconomic headwinds have further tightened global liquidity. Hotter-than-expected US consumer inflation readings have pushed the 10-year US Treasury yield past 5 per cent and prompted bond traders to price in the risk of renewed Federal Reserve interest rate increases rather than cuts. At the same time, shifting capital flows across the technology sector have drained speculative liquidity from digital tokens. FalconX co-head of markets Joshua Lim noted in commentary reported by Bloomberg that nearly $20 billion in stablecoin outflows over the past month, alongside investors raising cash for major artificial intelligence listings such as Anthropic’s market debut, have weighed heavily on crypto valuations. Derivatives markets reflect widespread defensive positioning as leveraged long bets unwind. More than $528 million in leveraged Bitcoin positions were liquidated during the latest leg down, while the crypto Fear and Greed Index dropped to 12, signalling extreme investor anxiety. Technical analysts warn that a sustained break below the $59, 800 to $60, 500 support band could expose Bitcoin to a test of its July 1 yearly low near $57, 877, with deeper weekly support sitting closer to $55, 000. Until Treasury yields stabilise and institutional exchange-traded fund outflows reverse, analysts expect Bitcoin to remain tethered to the broader trajectory of global equities.

By: Zaini Majeed Last Updated: November 21, 2026 00:24:26 IST

Bitcoin has plunged below the psychologically critical $60, 000 threshold to hit its weakest level since July, undermining long-standing claims that the world’s largest cryptocurrency functions as “digital gold” during periods of financial turbulence.

Trading around $59, 170 on Friday, Bitcoin has shed roughly $20, 000 over the past month alone and now sits approximately 53 per cent below its October 2025 record high near $126, 000. Far from shielding investor portfolios from equity volatility, the digital asset broke lower shortly after the US market open alongside sharp losses in technology shares, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 2. 4 per cent and chipmaker Nvidia dropping 6 per cent.

“The market appears to be trying to find a footing, ” Fairlead Strategies founder Katie Stockton said in a market note cited by financial outlets, pointing out that Bitcoin’s trading range has compressed to a floor just below $60, 000 as its correlation with the Nasdaq-100 climbed steadily since late September.

Proponents of cryptocurrency have argued for years that Bitcoin’s capped supply of 21 million coins makes it an uncorrelated store of value capable of insulating investors from inflation and stock market drawdowns. Recent cross-asset trading, however, indicates that institutional desks continue to treat Bitcoin as a high-beta risk asset rather than a defensive refuge.

Market data from Fairlead Strategies underscores that Bitcoin has moved largely in tandem with high-growth technology stocks throughout the autumn downturn. Even physical bullion faced acute liquidity pressure this week, with spot gold sliding more than 3 per cent to drop below $3, 700 per ounce as investors raised cash across asset classes to cover losses and margin requirements.

Corporate treasury buyers that fuelled earlier rallies are also magnifying the downward volatility. Cordoba Advisory Partners chief investment officer Abe Sheikh told market analysts that companies such as Strategy, which holds 850, 849 BTC, roughly 4 per cent of total supply, borrow capital to accumulate Bitcoin during upswings and face pressure to offload holdings to service debt obligations when prices retreat.

Institutional retreat from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds has removed a vital pillar of market support. According to figures compiled by Farside Investors, investors withdrew $582. 3 million from US spot Bitcoin funds on Thursday alone—including $541. 1 million from BlackRock’s flagship iShares fund—marking a third consecutive day of redemptions and pushing total November outflows to $3. 47 billion.

Broader macroeconomic headwinds have further tightened global liquidity. Hotter-than-expected US consumer inflation readings have pushed the 10-year US Treasury yield past 5 per cent and prompted bond traders to price in the risk of renewed Federal Reserve interest rate increases rather than cuts.

At the same time, shifting capital flows across the technology sector have drained speculative liquidity from digital tokens. FalconX co-head of markets Joshua Lim noted in commentary reported by Bloomberg that nearly $20 billion in stablecoin outflows over the past month, alongside investors raising cash for major artificial intelligence listings such as Anthropic’s market debut, have weighed heavily on crypto valuations.

Derivatives markets reflect widespread defensive positioning as leveraged long bets unwind. More than $528 million in leveraged Bitcoin positions were liquidated during the latest leg down, while the crypto Fear and Greed Index dropped to 12, signalling extreme investor anxiety.

Technical analysts warn that a sustained break below the $59, 800 to $60, 500 support band could expose Bitcoin to a test of its July 1 yearly low near $57, 877, with deeper weekly support sitting closer to $55, 000. Until Treasury yields stabilise and institutional exchange-traded fund outflows reverse, analysts expect Bitcoin to remain tethered to the broader trajectory of global equities.

extraction.body: Bitcoin fell sharply on Thursday, dropping below $85,000 for the first time in nearly two months, as a broad pullback in risk assets swept through global markets and intensified pressure on cryptocurrencies. The world’s largest digital asset slid as much as 5.7% to $84,233, its lowest level since Dec. 1. The decline marked a significant breakdown after weeks of sideways trading and underscored the fragility of sentiment across the crypto market. Losses were even steeper among smaller tokens, with Ether, XRP, Dogecoin, Cardano and Solana all falling by 6% or more. The sharp move lower in prices triggered a wave of forced selling across crypto derivatives markets. Around $785 million worth of digital assets were liquidated over the past 24 hours, according to data compiled by Coinglass. More than half of those liquidations occurred in just the last four hours, reflecting the speed at which losses cascaded as key technical levels were breached. The latest drop extended a broader downturn that has persisted in crypto markets since early October. Bitcoin prices had largely stagnated in recent weeks, even as technology stocks and precious metals such as gold and silver rallied. That divergence broke down abruptly, however, as cryptocurrencies began to mirror a wider selloff in risk assets. Technology stocks led the decline, with Microsoft shares collapsing more than 11%, a move that would rank as their worst one-day fall since March 2020. The selloff followed the company’s report of slowing growth in its cloud business and dragged the Nasdaq Composite lower by roughly 1.5%, reinforcing a risk-off tone across markets. The pressure was not limited to equities. Precious metals, which had surged to record highs, also reversed violently. Gold, which had briefly climbed above $5,600 per ounce earlier in the session — having never traded above $5,000 before Sunday night — plunged nearly 10% within minutes during US morning trade, falling back below $5,200. Silver followed a similar trajectory, sliding from around $121 per ounce to $108. Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have also come under strain. So far this week, bitcoin ETFs have recorded $160.1 million in net outflows, according to data from SoSoValue, extending a pattern of capital leaving the products amid market turbulence. Julio Moreno, head of research at CryptoQuant, said the recent pullback represents the first meaningful stress test for bitcoin ETFs since their rapid growth last year. Moreno noted that cumulative ETF flows peaked at $72.6 billion on Oct. 10, 2025, and have since seen $6.1 billion in net outflows. That reduction has cut ETF holdings to about $66.5 billion, representing an 8.4% drawdown from the peak. “If price holds above ETF realized price, it gives this cohort a reason to stay invested. If it fails, ETF flows risk shifting from passive consolidation into active distribution. Right now, Bitcoin is trading at the line where ETF conviction is tested,” Moreno wrote. passages: Bitcoin fell sharply on Thursday, dropping below $85,000 for the first time in nearly two months, as a broad pullback in risk assets swept through global markets and intensified pressure on cryptocurrencies.
The world’s largest digital asset slid as much as 5.7% to $84,233, its lowest level since Dec. 1.
The decline marked a significant breakdown after weeks of sideways trading and underscored the fragility of sentiment across the crypto market.
Losses were even steeper among smaller tokens, with Ether, XRP, Dogecoin, Cardano and Solana all falling by 6% or more.
The sharp move lower in prices triggered a wave of forced selling across crypto derivatives markets.
Around $785 million worth of digital assets were liquidated over the past 24 hours, according to data compiled by Coinglass.
More than half of those liquidations occurred in just the last four hours, reflecting the speed at which losses cascaded as key technical levels were breached.
The latest drop extended a broader downturn that has persisted in crypto markets since early October.
Bitcoin prices had largely stagnated in recent weeks, even as technology stocks and precious metals such as gold and silver rallied.
That divergence broke down abruptly, however, as cryptocurrencies began to mirror a wider selloff in risk assets.
Technology stocks led the decline, with Microsoft shares collapsing more than 11%, a move that would rank as their worst one-day fall since March 2020.
The selloff followed the company’s report of slowing growth in its cloud business and dragged the Nasdaq Composite lower by roughly 1.5%, reinforcing a risk-off tone across markets.
The pressure was not limited to equities. Precious metals, which had surged to record highs, also reversed violently.

Gold, which had briefly climbed above $5,600 per ounce earlier in the session — having never traded above $5,000 before Sunday night — plunged nearly 10% within minutes during US morning trade, falling back below $5,200.
Silver followed a similar trajectory, sliding from around $121 per ounce to $108.
Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have also come under strain.
So far this week, bitcoin ETFs have recorded $160.1 million in net outflows, according to data from SoSoValue, extending a pattern of capital leaving the products amid market turbulence.
Julio Moreno, head of research at CryptoQuant, said the recent pullback represents the first meaningful stress test for bitcoin ETFs since their rapid growth last year.
Moreno noted that cumulative ETF flows peaked at $72.6 billion on Oct. 10, 2025, and have since seen $6.1 billion in net outflows.
That reduction has cut ETF holdings to about $66.5 billion, representing an 8.4% drawdown from the peak.

“If price holds above ETF realized price, it gives this cohort a reason to stay invested. If it fails, ETF flows risk shifting from passive consolidation into active distribution. Right now, Bitcoin is trading at the line where ETF conviction is tested,” Moreno wrote.

Taken together, the cryptocurrency is failing the test again when it comes to showing its worth as a market hedge during times of investor anxiety.
Bitcoin 's latest sell-off is reviving doubts that it can behave as the "digital gold" market hedge that crypto backers have long envisioned.
Bitcoin was trading under $62,000 on Friday morning, down from an all-time high of more than $126,000 in early October last year.
Its downward spiral in recent months and weeks has been precipitated by a confluence of factors.

Bitcoin's rising correlation with the Nasdaq-100 since late September suggests the two are increasingly moving in tandem, according to data from Fairlead Strategies, a technical research firm.

"There's a bit more caution than there was a year ago." What is behind bitcoin's fall, and what is in store for its future? Here is what experts say. When rates are down and treasuries aren't paying good yields, people tend to be more risk-seeking for higher returns. "Bitcoin for many investors is in that bucket," Sanchez said. Experts have noted that gold, which is now down over 35% from its early 2026 peak, is less attractive when cash accounts are paying 5%. Investments like gold and bitcoin offer no yield. But it's also been caught up in monetary policy since its inception. The last decade or so of monetary policy has been extremely rewarding to speculative risk-on assets, Georgiades said. However, in periods of volatility, those types of assets have experienced the most significant drawdowns and have been the most heavily punished, Georgiades said. That means that a shock on one side of the board that might be completely independent of bitcoin could trigger a large volatility event "given how intertwined digital assets have become in the overall financial system," he said. Notably, bitcoin hasn't acted much like digital gold in more recent years, said Abe Sheikh, chief investment officer of Cordoba Advisory Partners in New York. In fact, it has fallen substantially during periods when the stock market has been falling. For example, from October 6 through November 18, the S&P 500 fell about 6.3%, and bitcoin fell around 27%. This fall, investors also started to question the security of encryption technology, leading to more concerns over the security of their bitcoin holdings, said Kirkley of Global Settlement Network. The Binance hack in October muddied the waters further. And the recent stock market jitters and economic concerns piled on doubts, Kirkley said. The last few weeks have been especially rough with data security concerns from multiple fronts, he added. Wall Street's embrace of bitcoin has been a big positive for the cryptocurrency. Kirkley noted that 20% of bitcoin's market price is coming from institutional investors, and that's a conservative estimate. In addition, new research from digital assets company Galaxy shows that a record 40.5% of all 13F-reported spot bitcoin exchange-traded product holdings, and 11.2% of all the bitcoin in the funds, came from advisory and wealth planning firms, such as RIAs and brokerage platforms, as of the third quarter 13F filings with the SEC, which are required of firms with over $100 million in assets to report their holdings. Much of this investment is through bitcoin spot ETFs like the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) that track its price. These ETFs, first approved by the SEC in January 2024, were supposed to provide a reliable new source of institutional demand. But ETF ownership also makes bitcoin especially easy to sell. Outflows from several of these funds have been substantial in recent months. IBIT, the largest of its peers, had six-month net outflows of $1.65 billion through Nov. 18 and one-month outflows of $1.37 billion, according to ETF Database. The second biggest, Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund ( FBTC ) had one-month net outflows of $322.65 million and six-month net outflows of $771.86 million, according to ETF Database. Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ETF ( BTC ) had one-month net outflows of $66.35 million, though it had inflows of $590.04 million over six months. As of September 2026, public companies collectively hold close to 1.29 million bitcoins, which is more than 6% of the 21 million coins in existence, according to bitcoin.com . Most public companies invest their corporate treasury portfolios in low-risk, highly liquid instruments such as money market funds, Treasury bonds and Treasury bills. That said, there are some well-known companies that have invested in bitcoin. SpaceX, for example, purchased 18,712 bitcoins for a total cost of $661 million, at an average price of $35,324 per coin. The company began accumulating bitcoin in early 2021 and held its position unchanged from mid-2024 until its IPO filing . Digital Asset Treasury companies, known as DATs or DATCOs, have also played a role in bitcoin's volatility . DATs are publicly listed firms whose primary business strategy involves holding significant quantities of digital assets, such as bitcoin or ethereum , on their corporate balance sheets to drive shareholder value. Companies in this space include Strategy , Strive, and Twenty One Capital. "DATs have exacerbated the problem," said Sheikh of Cordoba Advisory Partners. When bitcoin is rising, these companies borrow money in the debt market or raise capital to buy more bitcoin, which magnifies the upswings. They have also sold bitcoin to make their bond coupon payments. "It leads to enormous volatility on the upside and downside," Sheikh said. As of mid-November, Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, holds 850,849 BTC, according to a regulatory filing . That represents roughly 4% of bitcoin's total supply. The company acquired these holdings at a total cost of approximately $64.2 billion, with an average purchase price of roughly $75,452 per coin, according to the filing. Bitcoin has been trending lower since the peak in October 2025. A trading range has taken hold and the bottom of the range is just below 60,000, said Katie Stockton, founder and managing partner of Fairlead Strategies. "It appears to be trying to find a footing," she said. Oversold conditions on the heels of recent lows in June and July, in addition to long-term momentum, suggest bitcoin can support an upturn, she said. But that depends on whether the crypto can hold at a current range around $60,000, she said. "At the end of the day, bitcoin is exceptionally volatile. It's still an area that people might go to sell when they think that risk is higher in other areas." By mid-morning Friday, the price of bitcoin had slipped below $60,000, its lowest mark since July. It was on pace for its seventh-straight weekly loss for the first time since May 2022, according to CNBC data.

FalconX co-head of markets Joshua Lim noted in commentary reported by Bloomberg that nearly $20 billion in stablecoin outflows over the past month, alongside investors raising cash for major artificial intelligence listings such as Anthropic’s market debut, have weighed heavily on crypto valuations. Derivatives markets reflect widespread defensive positioning as leveraged long bets unwind. More than $528 million in leveraged Bitcoin positions were liquidated during the latest leg down, while the crypto Fear and Greed Index dropped to 12, signalling extreme investor anxiety. Technical analysts warn that a sustained break below the $59, 800 to $60, 500 support band could expose Bitcoin to a test of its July 1 yearly low near $57, 877, with deeper weekly support sitting closer to $55, 000. The world’s largest digital asset slid as much as 5.7% to $84,233, its lowest level since Dec. 1. The decline marked a significant breakdown after weeks of sideways trading and underscored the fragility of sentiment across the crypto market. Losses were even steeper among smaller tokens, with Ether, XRP, Dogecoin, Cardano and Solana all falling by 6% or more. The sharp move lower in prices triggered a wave of forced selling across crypto derivatives markets. Around $785 million worth of digital assets were liquidated over the past 24 hours, according to data compiled by Coinglass. More than half of those liquidations occurred in just the last four hours, reflecting the speed at which losses cascaded as key technical levels were breached. The latest drop extended a broader downturn that has persisted in crypto markets since early October. Bitcoin prices had largely stagnated in recent weeks, even as technology stocks and precious metals such as gold and silver rallied. That divergence broke down abruptly, however, as cryptocurrencies began to mirror a wider selloff in risk assets. The selloff followed the company’s report of slowing growth in its cloud business and dragged the Nasdaq Composite lower by roughly 1.5%, reinforcing a risk-off tone across markets. The pressure was not limited to equities. Precious metals, which had surged to record highs, also reversed violently. Gold, which had briefly climbed above $5,600 per ounce earlier in the session — having never traded above $5,000 before Sunday night — plunged nearly 10% within minutes during US morning trade, falling back below $5,200. Silver followed a similar trajectory, sliding from around $121 per ounce to $108. Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have also come under strain. So far this week, bitcoin ETFs have recorded $160.1 million in net outflows, according to data from SoSoValue, extending a pattern of capital leaving the products amid market turbulence. Julio Moreno, head of research at CryptoQuant, said the recent pullback represents the first meaningful stress test for bitcoin ETFs since their rapid growth last year. facts.text: But the market itself may be the biggest factor.
Investors are currently in sell everything mode, including tech stocks and gold — the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 tumbled into correction territory on Friday, according to CNBC data.
Bitcoin's recent price action has also tracked the move in the biggest tech IPOs , SpaceX and Anthropic.
Taken together, the cryptocurrency is failing the test again when it comes to showing its worth as a market hedge during times of investor anxiety.
Bitcoin 's latest sell-off is reviving doubts that it can behave as the "digital gold" market hedge that crypto backers have long envisioned.
Bitcoin was trading under $62,000 on Friday morning, down from an all-time high of more than $126,000 in early October last year.
Its downward spiral in recent months and weeks has been precipitated by a confluence of factors.
By mid-morning Friday, the price of bitcoin had slipped below $60,000, its lowest mark since July.
Notably, bitcoin hasn't acted much like digital gold in more recent years, said Abe Sheikh, chief investment officer of Cordoba Advisory Partners in New York.
Bitcoin has been trending lower since the peak in October 2025.
"It appears to be trying to find a footing," she said.
Bitcoin's rising correlation with the Nasdaq-100 since late September suggests the two are increasingly moving in tandem, according to data from Fairlead Strategies, a technical research firm.
That's consistent with an environment of higher volatility in which correlations across risk assets tend to increase.
However, the correlation remains below its early-2026 highs, the data show.

extraction.body: Bitcoin’s price plunged below $59,000 on Friday as the November cryptocurrency market rout showed no signs of letting up. The plunge came just days after crypto market maker Wintermute warned that bitcoin’s bear market was not over and flagged the risk of a further slide into the $50,000 range. Bitstamp data shows bitcoin briefly dropped to $58,701, a level last seen in early July, when a bearish trend threatened to push the price toward $50,000. Earlier Friday, however, bitcoin appeared to be holding comfortably above $61,000, with $62,000 acting as its immediate resistance level. Between 11 a.m. and noon EST, bitcoin shed nearly $3,000 amid heightened selling pressure and a lack of buyers. Although a relief rally briefly lifted the price above $59,300, the cryptocurrency was still down approximately 5% over 24 hours and more than 13% over seven days. After narrowing its year-to-date losses to single digits by the end of September, bitcoin has steadily declined since the beginning of October. The latest sell-off leaves the cryptocurrency down more than 30% since Jan. 1. Meanwhile, bitcoin’s sharp decline was particularly devastating for traders betting on higher prices. According to Coinglass data, the price collapse wiped out more than $220 million in leveraged long positions in just one hour, compared with less than $10 million in short positions. Over 24 hours, bitcoin liquidations exceeded $543 million, including more than $494 million in long positions. With most major altcoins mirroring bitcoin’s decline, long liquidations across the broader cryptocurrency market surpassed $1.38 billion over 24 hours, while short liquidations totaled approximately $142 million—a total of $1.53 billion in liquidations across the market. In its Nov. 16 market update, Wintermute argued that bitcoin’s recent rebounds were primarily driven by short covering rather than fresh spot buying. Without renewed demand from spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which have recorded roughly $1.9 billion in net outflows in 2026, and corporate bitcoin treasury companies, the prospects for a sustained recovery remain slim. Wintermute said bitcoin would need to reclaim $68,000 on a sustained basis, accompanied by a clear return to net spot ETF inflows, before the market maker would reconsider its bearish outlook. The cryptocurrency market sell-off came on the heels of Anthropic’s record-breaking initial public offering (IPO), which raised more than $81 billion. However, the blockbuster listing failed to revive investor confidence in technology stocks, which have been battered by mounting concerns over artificial intelligence valuations, the profitability of massive AI infrastructure investments and the prospect of further U.S. interest rate hikes. The pressure intensified Friday as Anthropic shares plunged almost 13% following their trading debut, while semiconductor stocks extended their losses. Nvidia fell approximately 7% in morning trading, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) dropped nearly 12%. Broadcom, Marvell Technology, and Micron Technology each shed more than 9%, underscoring the scale of the sell-off in companies closely tied to the AI boom. The rout also reflected growing doubts about whether the billions of dollars being poured into AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns to justify elevated technology stock valuations. Nvidia’s recent leadership upheaval, regulatory uncertainty following the U.S. midterm elections and concerns about higher borrowing costs have further undermined investor confidence. Adding to the pressure, hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials have reinforced expectations of another interest rate hike in December. Higher borrowing costs typically weigh on growth-oriented technology companies by reducing the present value of their expected future earnings and making speculative investments less attractive. The resulting sell-off pushed the Nasdaq down approximately 3.5% on Friday, while the broader S&P 500 fell 2%. The S&P 500 was heading toward its seventh consecutive losing session, while the Nasdaq briefly slipped into negative territory for the year. The simultaneous decline in bitcoin, technology stocks, and other risk-sensitive assets suggests that investors are increasingly reducing exposure to speculative investments amid mounting uncertainty over valuations, monetary policy, and economic growth.

Bitstamp data shows bitcoin briefly dropped to $58,701, a level last seen in early July, when a bearish trend threatened to push the price toward $50,000. Earlier Friday, however, bitcoin appeared to be holding comfortably above $61,000, with $62,000 acting as its immediate resistance level. Between 11 a.m. and noon EST, bitcoin shed nearly $3,000 amid heightened selling pressure and a lack of buyers. Although a relief rally briefly lifted the price above $59,300, the cryptocurrency was still down approximately 5% over 24 hours and more than 13% over seven days. After narrowing its year-to-date losses to single digits by the end of September, bitcoin has steadily declined since the beginning of October. The latest sell-off leaves the cryptocurrency down more than 30% since Jan. 1. Meanwhile, bitcoin’s sharp decline was particularly devastating for traders betting on higher prices. According to Coinglass data, the price collapse wiped out more than $220 million in leveraged long positions in just one hour, compared with less than $10 million in short positions. Over 24 hours, bitcoin liquidations exceeded $543 million, including more than $494 million in long positions. With most major altcoins mirroring bitcoin’s decline, long liquidations across the broader cryptocurrency market surpassed $1.38 billion over 24 hours, while short liquidations totaled approximately $142 million—a total of $1.53 billion in liquidations across the market. In its Nov. 16 market update, Wintermute argued that bitcoin’s recent rebounds were primarily driven by short covering rather than fresh spot buying. Without renewed demand from spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which have recorded roughly $1.9 billion in net outflows in 2026, and corporate bitcoin treasury companies, the prospects for a sustained recovery remain slim. Wintermute said bitcoin would need to reclaim $68,000 on a sustained basis, accompanied by a clear return to net spot ETF inflows, before the market maker would reconsider its bearish outlook. The cryptocurrency market sell-off came on the heels of Anthropic’s record-breaking initial public offering (IPO), which raised more than $81 billion. However, the blockbuster listing failed to revive investor confidence in technology stocks, which have been battered by mounting concerns over artificial intelligence valuations, the profitability of massive AI infrastructure investments and the prospect of further U.S. interest rate hikes. The pressure intensified Friday as Anthropic shares plunged almost 13% following their trading debut, while semiconductor stocks extended their losses. Nvidia fell approximately 7% in morning trading, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) dropped nearly 12%. Broadcom, Marvell Technology, and Micron Technology each shed more than 9%, underscoring the scale of the sell-off in companies closely tied to the AI boom. The rout also reflected growing doubts about whether the billions of dollars being poured into AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns to justify elevated technology stock valuations. Nvidia’s recent leadership upheaval, regulatory uncertainty following the U.S. midterm elections and concerns about higher borrowing costs have further undermined investor confidence. Adding to the pressure, hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials have reinforced expectations of another interest rate hike in December. Higher borrowing costs typically weigh on growth-oriented technology companies by reducing the present value of their expected future earnings and making speculative investments less attractive. The resulting sell-off pushed the Nasdaq down approximately 3.5% on Friday, while the broader S&P 500 fell 2%. The S&P 500 was heading toward its seventh consecutive losing session, while the Nasdaq briefly slipped into negative territory for the year. The simultaneous decline in bitcoin, technology stocks, and other risk-sensitive assets suggests that investors are increasingly reducing exposure to speculative investments amid mounting uncertainty over valuations, monetary policy, and economic growth.

extraction.body: The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower. Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data . The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000. The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss. Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower. Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry. Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed . Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield. Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin. Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027. JUST IN: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 for the first time since June. BTC is now less than 4% away from a new cycle low 👀 pic.twitter.com/GSZkbGdzZz Funds have been sellers. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1 million on Thursday, its biggest one-day outflow on record. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total, extending a streak of heavy withdrawals this week. Leveraged traders were hit as well. More than $700 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the 24 hours before the latest drop, and about 86% were bets on higher prices. The slide below $60,000 likely forced out more of them. The move extends a month-long slump. Bitcoin has dropped roughly $20,000 in the past month, a slide tracked as the price fell under $62,000 on Thursday. Crypto stocks fell even faster. Strategy (MSTR) was down about 7% near $79.85, a day after it tumbled for a sixth straight session . Coinbase (COIN) fell about 3% to $105.36. Shares of Strive (ASST) fell to $15.31 Friday morning, down 21.47%, or $4.19, over the past five days. The stock has slid steadily from near $19.50 as bitcoin price’s sell-off deepened, with its sharpest drop in Friday’s trading. Bitcoin miners took the worst of it. MARA Holdings (MARA) dropped about 11% to $5.55. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 11% to $15.85, and CleanSpark (CLSK) fell about 12% to $5.13. Data center operators that also mine bitcoin were hit hard. IREN fell about 12% to $12.62, and Cipher Digital (CIFR) dropped 14% to $5.58. Both have traded with AI stocks, which are also under pressure. The bitcoin price is now at its lowest since the first days of July. Bitcoin set its record above $126,000 in October 2025, so it has lost more than half its value from that peak. At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $59,600.
